original_question: A 51-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 1-day history of right flank pain and bloody urine. Over the past 2 weeks, she has also developed progressive lower extremity swelling and a 3-kg (7-lb) weight gain. She has a history of chronic hepatitis B infection, which was diagnosed 10 years ago. She frequently flies from California to New York for business. She appears fatigued. Her pulse is 98/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 135/75 mm Hg. Examination shows periorbital edema, a distended abdomen, and 2+ edema of the lower extremities. The lungs are clear to auscultation. A CT scan of the abdomen shows a nodular liver with ascites, a large right kidney with abundant collateral vessels, and a filling defect in the right renal vein. Urinalysis shows 4+ protein, positive glucose, and fatty casts. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's renal vein findings?

base.stage_1: A 51-year-old woman presents to the clinic complaining of right flank pain and bloody urine for the past day.
base.stage_2: The patient reports progressive lower extremity swelling and a 3-kg weight gain over the past two weeks. She appears fatigued. Her pulse is 98/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 135/75 mm Hg. Physical examination reveals periorbital edema, a distended abdomen, and 2+ edema of the lower extremities. Her lungs are clear to auscultation.
base.stage_3: The patient has a history of chronic hepatitis B infection and frequently flies for business. A CT scan of the abdomen shows a nodular liver with ascites, a large right kidney with abundant collateral vessels, and a filling defect in the right renal vein. Urinalysis shows 4+ protein, positive glucose, and fatty casts.
base.stage_4: Further laboratory testing reveals a significantly decreased level of antithrombin III activity. Genetic testing confirms a heterozygous mutation in the SERPINC1 gene, consistent with hereditary antithrombin III deficiency.

counterfactuals.alteration_description: The patient reports pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath, which argues against antithrombin III deficiency, which typically presents with venous thromboembolism, not pulmonary embolism.
